owner.occupation: Foreign English lecturer at a Lanzhou university

world.bio: From Dayton, Ohio. Sixth year teaching oral English and academic writing at a university in Lanzhou. I eat beef noodles every morning at the same place near the west gate, and I've carried my fourteen-year-old golden retriever, Biscuit, through two international moves: Ohio to Chengdu, then Chengdu to Lanzhou. My Chinese is decent in restaurants and bad in hospitals.
skills_assets: Six years of university-level English teaching in China
TEFL certificate and a master's in applied linguistics from Ohio State
Chinese at about HSK 4, conversational but not technical
A small apartment near campus, dog-friendly landlord
Social circle among foreign teachers in Gansu, about fifteen people
A blog about teaching in Lanzhou with a few hundred readers

projects.name: Dunhuang winter trip
projects.text: Planning a five-day trip to Dunhuang in January, flying from Lanzhou to Jiayuguan then train. I want to see the Mogao caves in winter without the crowds. Haven't booked anything because I'm waiting to see how Biscuit does.

projects.name: Spring course design
projects.text: Preparing a new elective on 'English for science writing' for the spring term. Syllabus due December 5.

notes.text: Biscuit isn't eating much lately and breathes heavy at night, she's fourteen. I've been telling myself that's just age. This morning she left half her breakfast, which she has never done in her life.
Took Biscuit to a clinic near campus. The vet said 'just old'. Gave me a bag of supplements. I asked about the heavy breathing, he shrugged. My Chinese isn't good enough for a real argument.
Beef noodles at 7:30 as usual. The owner now gives me extra beef when she sees me. She asked about Biscuit. I said she's tired. She said, 'Old dogs get tired.' I wanted to hug her.

Second clinic, different part of town. They did a blood test and an X-ray. A young vet said something quickly, and I caught the word 'heart', or maybe 'old heart'. He suggested we 'consider whether she's suffering', which is a polite way to say euthanasia. I took the report home. It's in Chinese, full of numbers and abbreviations I can't read.
Spent an hour with the report and a translation app. The app turns 'cardiac enlargement' into something like 'heart is big'. I don't know what to ask. I don't know what to do.

Brother Mark called. We argued about Mom's care home again, $5,800 a month. He wants to move her to a cheaper one in Cincinnati. I said I'd pay a share. He said, 'You live in China, how can you pay?' Hung up on each other.
Class went badly. Student asked about the idiom 'barking up the wrong tree' and I thought about Biscuit for the rest of the lecture. Dismissed early.
Walked Biscuit in the Yellow River park. She walked slowly, stopped twice, looked at me. I sat on a bench and she put her head on my knee.
Winter trip is probably cancelled. I can't leave her. I told my friend Jess I wasn't sure about travel. She said, 'Is it the dog?' I said, yes, and then couldn't speak.

messages.text: Jess: How's Biscuit? Caleb: Not great. Jess: Have you found a good vet? Caleb: Two so far. Jess: Which hospital? Caleb: Neither speaks English.
Wang: Mr. Hartwell, you seem tired. Caleb: Sorry, my dog is unwell. Wang: Do you want me to call a vet? Caleb: I'd appreciate it. Wang: I will ask my neighbour.
Mark: Are you in or out on Mom's care? Caleb: In. Mark: With what money? Caleb: I'll send $500 a month. Mark: That's not enough. Caleb: It's what I have.
Landlord: The dog is old. Are you okay? Caleb: Trying. Landlord: If she needs anything, I'll help. Caleb: Thank you.
Mom: How's Biscuit? Caleb: Not good. Mom: She was such a good girl. Caleb: She still is.

relations.about: In Ohio, handles Mom's care, tension over money.
14-year-old golden retriever, the most important being in his life.

constraints: Cannot leave Lanzhou for long while Biscuit is unwell
Chinese isn't good enough for medical terminology
Budget limit of about 5,000 RMB for vet bills this month
Teaching schedule is rigid on Monday to Thursday
sensitive: Terrified of losing Biscuit; she was with him through his divorce
